data.summary: Dec soybean meal settled $345.70/st on 23 Nov, a 20-session high and up $25 from 9 Nov; Jan soybeans rose 8¢ to $12.28¾ as weekly US soybean inspections hit 1.555 Mt (China 775,700 t). Dec corn slipped ¼¢ to $4.34¼ and SRW wheat rose 2¾¢ to $5.77.
data.title: CBOT 23 Nov: Dec meal settles $345.70 (+$4.70), Jan soybeans +8¢ on China buying

data.summary: The median of 13 Punjab mandis rose to Rs5,550 per 40 kg (Rs13,875 per 100 kg) on 24 Nov from Rs12,500 on 23 Nov, 32% above 1 Sep; Jauharabad, Chichawatni and Kamalia traded at Rs5,650–5,700 per 40 kg.
data.title: AMIS wheat 24 Nov: Punjab median jumps 11% to Rs13,875 per 100 kg

data.act: Lock Dec–Jan needs this week with at least two crushers holding bean stocks before they reprice to the $346 CBOT level; a licence lapse at end-November would tighten local supply further.
data.why: CBOT Dec meal settled $345.70/st on 23 Nov, up $4.70 from 20 Nov and $25.00 (7.8%) above 9 Nov ($320.70), with Jan soybeans up 8¢ to $12.28¾ on strong China buying (775,700 t of 1.555 Mt inspected last week). Pakistan still buys meal from local crushers only: import approvals were deferred on 23 Oct and current GM soybean licences run only through November 2026, with no renewal found as of 24 Nov.

data.act: Cover winter wanda needs for 30–45 days this week with quotes from two flour mills, in one lot rather than tranches, before mills reprice bran to the new wheat level.
data.why: AMIS Punjab wheat median jumped 11% to Rs138.8/kg on 24 Nov (13 mandis, Rs5,550 per 40 kg) from Rs125.0/kg on 23 Nov and is 32% above 1 Sep. Karachi fine flour rose Rs20 to Rs210/kg on 23 Nov and TCP's third 800,000 t import tender closes 30 Nov, so bran stays tight through winter until the April harvest.
